Belgian Waffle Ride California

04.25 Del Mar

What is the Belgian Waffle Ride California?

Belgian Waffle Ride California is a mixed-surface ‘unroad’ race that starts and finishes at the Del Mar Polo Fields at Surf Sports Park in Del Mar, north of San Diego, in late April or early May. The 106.5-mile Waffle carries about 7,500 feet of climbing and 30 sectors of sand, dirt and singletrack; the Wafer (60 miles) and Wanna (32.7 miles) are shorter. Michael Marckx started it in 2012, and it is now the California stop of the Quad-Tripel Crown of Gravel series. The next edition is listed for April 25, 2027.

How the Belgian Waffle Ride California started

Michael Marckx started the Belgian Waffle Ride in North San Diego County as a Belgian-classic-style day of pavement and dirt bracketed by waffles and beer. The organizers count 2026 as the 15th annual California edition, which puts the first ride in 2012. It is produced by Monuments of Cycling, which now also runs BWR events in Arizona, Utah, Montana and Mexico.

For 2025 the California event moved to the Del Mar Polo Fields at Surf Sports Park, next to the Del Mar Fairgrounds and close to the coast, and became a three-day festival with a Saturday road gran fondo (the Gran Roadie-Oh) and an Unroad Expo before Sunday’s main ride. That year BWR also launched the Quad-Tripel Crown of Gravel series and added Bozeman, Montana.

The 2026 ride, May 2–3, marked the 15th anniversary with a new route that reached toward the Boden Canyon Ecological Reserve between Escondido and Ramona. Daxton Mock and Cécile Lejeune (both Trek Driftless) won the Waffle.

What to expect on the day

Saturday is the Gran Roadie-Oh, a road gran fondo with 24-, 66- and 100-mile options, plus the Unroad Expo at the polo fields. Sunday is the Belgian Waffle Ride itself, with Waffle men starting at 8:30 a.m. in 2026, followed by women’s waves and the other categories.

The Waffle is roughly 107 miles with about 7,450–7,500 feet of climbing and around 30 unroad sectors: deep sand, rock, doubletrack, fire road and singletrack, strung together by canyon climbs inland from the coast. Tire choice matters more than at most gravel races; the sand and rock punish narrow rubber.

The Wafer (60 miles) and Wanna (32.7 miles) hit a subset of the same sectors. All routes start and finish on the grass at the polo fields, where the waffles and Belgian-style beer are served.

Weather in Del Mar for the Belgian Waffle Ride California

Del Mar on the coast is mild in late April and May: average high about 69°F, low about 58°F, with under one rainy day in the month. The course runs inland into the canyons, where afternoons are noticeably hotter and drier than at the start.

The town

Sleep, eat, fix the bike.

Del Mar is a small beach city of about 4,000 people on the coast of San Diego County, roughly 21 miles north of San Diego International Airport. It is best known for the Del Mar Fairgrounds and its summer horse racing, and since 2025 it has hosted the Belgian Waffle Ride California at the Del Mar Polo Fields at Surf Sports Park, next door to the fairgrounds. Cyclists come for BWR and for the coast road and the canyons inland.

Fly into San Diego International (SAN), about 21 miles south; the drive up I-5 takes 25 to 35 minutes depending on traffic. Los Angeles is about two hours north by car. You will want a car in Del Mar, since the village, the polo fields and the Solana Beach bike shops are spread along a few miles of coast, though a bike covers it too.

Belgian Waffle Ride California FAQ

Where does it start?

At the Del Mar Polo Fields at Surf Sports Park in Del Mar, next to the Del Mar Fairgrounds, about 21 miles north of San Diego International Airport.

Is it a gravel race?

BWR calls it ‘unroad’: pavement plus dirt, sand, rock and singletrack. The Waffle is about 40 percent off pavement.

How long are the courses?

Waffle 106.5 miles (about 7,500 ft of climbing), Wafer 60 miles (about 3,750 ft), Wanna 32.7 miles (about 2,500 ft).

When is the 2027 edition?

The organizer’s future-dates page lists April 25, 2027. Venue and full schedule were not yet posted as of September 2026.

What bike should I ride?

A gravel bike with wide tires is the norm. The sand and rock sectors are the reason.

Is there a road option?

Yes. The Saturday Gran Roadie-Oh offers 24, 66 and 100 miles on pavement.
